assignedReviews.card_evidence: The abbreviation for centimeter is "cm"!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about describing science process skills (observing, predicting, measuring) and using units such as centimeter. The card only teaches the abbreviation 'cm' for centimeter. It does not describe any process skill or how to measure; it is a vocabulary fact about a unit, not direct instructional support for the skill of measuring.

copy.en:
What is the short way to write centimeter?

The abbreviation for centimeter is "cm"! Just two little letters to measure things.
copy.tl:
Ano ang maikling paraan para isulat ang sentimetro?

Ang daglat ng sentimetro ay "cm"! Dalawang maliit na letra lang para sukatin ang mga bagay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mubo nga paagi sa pagsulat sa sentimetro?

Ang minubo nga simbolo sa sentimetro kay "cm"! Duha ra ka gamay nga letra para pagsukod sa mga butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One centimeter equals exactly 10 millimeters.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches a unit conversion fact (1 cm = 10 mm), which is background knowledge for measuring, but it does not describe science process skills such as observing, predicting, or measuring, nor does it demonstrate the act of measuring with these units.

copy.en: Look closely at your ruler! One centimeter equals exactly 10 millimeters. Count them yourself!
copy.tl: Tumingin nang mabuti sa ruler mo! Isang sentimetro ay katumbas ng 10 milimetro. Bilangin mo!
copy.bis: Tan-awa pag-ayo ang imong ruler! Usa ka sentimetro parehas sa 10 ka milimetro. Ihap nimo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The symbol for centimeter is "cm"!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the symbol for centimeter. The competency requires describing science process skills such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units. Knowing the symbol is background knowledge for measuring but does not itself describe any process skill or demonstrate measuring.

copy.en: The symbol for centimeter is "cm"! You see it all the time on your school rulers.
copy.tl: Ang simbolo para sa sentimetro ay "cm"! Madalas itong makita sa mga ruler.
copy.bis: Ang simbolo para sa sentimetro kay "cm"! Kanunay kini makita sa mga ruler.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can grow a new one back as it grows and molts its skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth and molting, but its main point is regeneration of a lost leg, not describing the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can grow a new one back as it grows and molts its skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about leg regeneration in centipedes/millipedes, with no mention of cells, mitosis, meiosis, or cell division for growth and repair. It does not support the cellular reproduction competency.

copy.en: If a centipede or millipede loses a leg, it can grow a new one back as it grows and molts its skin.
copy.tl: Kapag nawalan ng paa ang alupihan o millipede, kaya nitong patubuin muli ang bagong paa habang lumalaki at nagpapalit ito ng balat.
copy.bis: Kung mawad-an og tiil ang alupihan o millipede, makapatubo kini og bag-o samtang kini modako ug mag-ilis og panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they come out and hunt for food mostly after dark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hunting for food but does not group centipedes as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it describe their diet. It only states they hunt at night.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they come out and hunt for food mostly after dark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or gathering food. It only mentions nocturnal hunting behavior.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they come out and hunt for food mostly after dark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: Nocturnal activity is a behavioral trait, but the card does not describe how centipedes have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not directly support the adaptation competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they come out and hunt for food mostly after dark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies centipedes depend on the environment for food, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is only a simple statement about hunting at night.

copy.en: Centipedes are night owls of the bug world — they come out and hunt for food mostly after dark.
copy.tl: Ang alupihan ay mas aktibo kapag gabi — lumalabas ito at naghahanap ng pagkain sa dilim.
copy.bis: Mas aktibo ang alupihan kon gabii — mogawas kini ug mangita og pagkaon sa kangitngit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the force directed toward the center of a circle that pulls an object to follow its curved path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples of accelerating objects at school and in the local community, including objects that show uniform circular motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines centripetal force and its direction, which is conceptually related to circular motion, but it does not ask students to observe or describe examples of accelerating objects at school or in the local community, nor does it mention uniform circular motion or acceleration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the force directed toward the center of a circle that pulls an object to follow its curved path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate in practical situations and describe that acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction as the result of a net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a force that changes direction, which is related to acceleration as a change in direction, but it does not demonstrate or describe acceleration as a result of a net force in practical situations. It only states the centripetal force concept without linking it to net force or acceleration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Centripetal force! It is the force directed toward the center of a circle that pulls an object to follow its curved path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a force, but it does not address that forces act between objects or that forces can be measured. It only names centripetal force and its direction, which is not direct support for the competency's focus on force measurement and interaction.

copy.en:
What pulls an object to keep it moving in a circle?

Centripetal force! It is the force directed toward the center of a circle that pulls an object to follow its curved path.
copy.tl:
Ano ang humihila sa isang bagay para manatili sa pabilog na landas?

Centripetal force! Ito ang puwersang nakaturo papunta sa gitna ng bilog na humihila sa bagay para manatili sa pabilog nitong landas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagbira sa butang aron magpabilin sa iyang lingin nga agianan?

Centripetal force! Mao kini ang puwersa nga nagtumong ngadto sa tunga sa lingin nga nagbira sa butang aron magpabilin sa kurba nga agianan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Squid and cuttlefish use copper instead of iron to carry oxygen in their blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Copper vs iron blood color is trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
What color is squid blood?

Bluish! Squid and cuttlefish use copper instead of iron to carry oxygen in their blood.
copy.tl:
Anong kulay ang dugo ng pusit?

Mamula-asul! Gumagamit ang pusit at kibet ng tanso, hindi bakal, para magdala ng oksiheno sa dugo.
copy.bis:
Unsay kolor sa dugo sa nokus?

Asul! Ang nokus ug kibot naggamit og tumbaga, dili puthaw, aron magdala og oksiheno sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many plates, cups, and dishes are made of ceramic because it is very clean to use for food!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies ceramic dishes as useful items made from a non-living material, but it does not describe what natural materials (e.g., clay) are used to make them. The competency requires both identifying the useful item and describing the natural materials, so the card only touches the first part without the required material description.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many plates, cups, and dishes are made of ceramic because it is very clean to use for food!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ceramic as a solid material but does not describe its physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The cleanliness attribute is not a physical property in the sense of the competency, and no property of the solid material is described.

copy.en:
Why are plates and cups made of ceramic?

Many plates, cups, and dishes are made of ceramic because it is very clean to use for food!
copy.tl:
Bakit ang mga pinggan at tasa ay gawa sa seramika?

Maraming pinggan, tasa, at plato ay gawa sa seramika dahil malinis itong gamitin sa pagkain!
copy.bis:
Nganong ang mga pinggan ug tasa hinimo sa seramika?

Daghang pinggan, tasa, ug plato hinimo sa seramika kay limpyo kini gamiton sa pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neutrons from one fission cause more fissions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions neutrons but does not differentiate protons, neutrons, and electrons by symbol, mass, charge, or location. It only uses neutrons in the context of a nuclear chain reaction, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neutrons from one fission cause more fissions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe or draw the structure of an atom (nucleus and electron shells). It only refers to neutrons and fission, which is unrelated to drawing atomic structure.

copy.en:
What happens when one tiny atom split starts a domino effect?

That's a chain reaction! Neutrons from one fission cause more fissions, keeping the process going!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag ang isang maliit na paghiwa ng atom ay nagsisimula ng domino effect?

Iyan ang chain reaction! Ang mga neutron mula sa isang fission ay nagdudulot ng dagdag pang fission, patuloy na nagpapatakbo sa proseso!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung ang usa ka gamay nga pagbahin sa atom mosugod ug domino effect?

Mao na ang chain reaction! Ang mga neutron gikan sa usa ka fission maghimo ug dugang nga mga fission, nagpadayon sa proseso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they need the right warmth, special lights, and live insects for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food, warmth, and light as needs of a chameleon, but it does not teach the general basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is pet-care advice for one animal, not a lesson on identifying universal basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they need the right warmth, special lights, and live insects for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions warmth and light, which are abiotic factors, and live insects, which are biotic, but it does not describe or classify living things as biotic factors or non-living things as abiotic factors in an ecosystem. It is about pet care, not ecosystem factor classification.

copy.en: Chameleons can be pets, but they're tricky — they need the right warmth, special lights, and live insects for food, so they're not for beginners.
copy.tl: Puwedeng alagaan ang chameleon, pero mahirap ito — kailangan nito ng tamang init, espesyal na ilaw, at buhay na insekto bilang pagkain, kaya hindi ito para sa baguhan.
copy.bis: Mahimong binuhi ang chameleon, apan lisod kini atimanon — kinahanglan niini ang husto nga kainit, espesyal nga suga, ug buhing insekto isip pagkaon, mao nga dili kini para sa bag-ohan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny crystals in its skin move closer together or farther apart, changing how light bounces off
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the physical mechanism of color change but does not describe how the chameleon has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention camouflage, mimicry, or any adaptive benefit. It shares the classic example organism but lacks the environmental-adaptation content the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: changing how light bounces off — and that changes the color we see
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses light reflection changing perceived color, not waves carrying energy from a source to a receiver. There is no source, receiver, or energy-transfer concept taught, so this does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: changing how light bounces off — and that changes the color we see
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: Light is mentioned as reflecting off crystals, but the card does not identify sources or uses of light energy at school, home, or community. It only uses light as part of a biological color-change explanation, so it is not direct support.

copy.en:
How does a chameleon change color?

Tiny crystals in its skin move closer together or farther apart, changing how light bounces off — and that changes the color we see.
copy.tl:
Paano nagbabago ng kulay ang chameleon?

Ang mga napakaliit na kristal sa balat nito ay tumitikom o lumuluwang, nagbabago ang pagsalamin ng liwanag dito — kaya nagbabago rin ang kulay na nakikita natin.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-usab og kolor sa chameleon?

Ang gagmay kaayo nga kristal sa iyang panit mosuod o molayo, mausab ang pagsalamin sa kahayag niini — mao nga mausab usab ang kolor nga atong makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chameleon's tail is called prehensile — it can curl and grip like a hand, keeping the chameleon from falling on thin branches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (tail) and its role (gripping to prevent falling), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. Gripping for stability is neither movement nor food gathering, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chameleon's tail is called prehensile — it can curl and grip like a hand, keeping the chameleon from falling on thin branches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a structural adaptation (prehensile tail) that helps the chameleon survive in its environment, but it does not describe how the animal has changed over time to better suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources. It is a single present-day feature, not an example of evolutionary change like mimicry or camouflage.

copy.en:
What is special about a chameleon's tail?

A chameleon's tail is called prehensile — it can curl and grip like a hand, keeping the chameleon from falling on thin branches.
copy.tl:
Ano ang espesyal sa buntot ng chameleon?

Tinatawag na prehensile ang buntot ng chameleon — kaya itong pumulupot at kumapit gaya ng kamay, para hindi ito mahulog sa manipis na sanga.
copy.bis:
Unsa'y espesyal sa ikog sa chameleon?

Gitawag kining prehensile ang ikog sa chameleon — makahimo kini molikos ug mokupot sama sa kamot, aron dili kini mahulog sa nipis nga sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: curling it around a branch so it won't fall!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the chameleon's tail as an outer body part and its role in gripping a branch, but the competency specifically requires identifying roles for movement and gathering food. The tail's function here is balance/gripping, not movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does a chameleon use its tail?

A chameleon uses its tail like a hand — curling it around a branch so it won't fall!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagamit ng chameleon ang buntot nito?

Ginagamit ng chameleon ang buntot nitong parang kamay — pumupulupot ito sa sanga para hindi mahulog!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paggamit sa chameleon ang iyang ikog?

Gigamit sa chameleon ang iyang ikog nga sama sa kamot — molambod kini sa sanga aron dili mahulog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Force can change the state of an object, making a resting object move or a moving object come to rest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force changing an object's state of motion, which is physics content. G6-E-7 requires demonstrating Earth's rotation on its axis using a globe to explain day and night; the card provides no support for this Earth/space competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Force can change the state of an object, making a resting object move or a moving object come to rest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses force and motion, not the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars moving across the sky. It does not support G3-E-7's guided exploration and recording of celestial objects.

copy.en: Force can change the state of an object, making a resting object move or a moving object come to rest.
copy.tl: Maaaring baguhin ng force ang estado ng isang bagay, ginagawang gumalaw ang nakahimpil na bagay o huminto ang gumagalaw na bagay.
copy.bis: Ang force makapausab sa kahimtang sa usa ka butang, nga makapalihok sa nagpahulay nga butang o makapahunong sa naglihok nga butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A change in an object's velocity or mass causes a change in its momentum.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about momentum change, not about wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) as described in G6-F-6. The topic is unrelated to waves.

copy.en: A change in an object's velocity or mass causes a change in its momentum.
copy.tl: Ang pagbabago sa velocity o mass ng isang bagay ay nagdudulot ng pagbabago sa momentum nito.
copy.bis: Ang pagbag-o sa velocity o mass sa usa ka butang maoy hinungdan sa pagbag-o sa momentum niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charcoal is almost pure carbon! When it is made, the water and other substances are driven out of the wood.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how charcoal is produced from wood, not changes in properties when materials are exposed to temperature changes such as burning wood or coal. It does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charcoal is almost pure carbon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card states charcoal is almost pure carbon, touching on the idea of a pure substance, but it does not describe fixed chemical composition, elements vs. compounds, or unique proton numbers. It only mentions carbon as a component, not the properties of pure substances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it is made, the water and other substances are driven out of the wood.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a process of removing substances from wood, but it does not explain why physical changes are reversible or chemical changes are irreversible. It does not address reversibility or the nature of the change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charcoal is almost pure carbon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions carbon, a chemical element, but does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Charcoal is almost pure carbon! When it is made, the water and other substances are driven out of the wood.
copy.tl: Ang uling ay halos purong carbon! Natanggal na ang tubig at iba pang sangkap mula sa kahoy noong ginawa ito.
copy.bis: Ang uling halos puro nga carbon! Nawala na ang tubig ug uban pang sangkap gikan sa kahoy dihang gihimo kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: trust a library book, museum card, or named interview more than an unsourced blog post
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives generic advice about preferring reliable sources for class projects. It does not address indigenous Philippine knowledge, eclipses, night sky patterns, or time tracking, which are the core subjects of G6-E-10.

copy.en: For class projects, trust a library book, museum card, or named interview more than an unsourced blog post you can't check!
copy.tl: Para sa proyekto, mas tiwalaan mo ang aklat sa library, museum card, o pangalanang interview kaysa sa blog na walang mapagkukunan!
copy.bis: Para sa proyekto, mas saligan nimo ang libro sa library, museum card, o gi-nganlan nga interview kay sa blog nga walay tinubdan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: protect the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that farming and plant science lessons are added so students learn to grow food sustainably and protect the environment. It mentions environmental protection but does not teach the concept that the environment must be protected and conserved for living things to survive. The card is a general rationale for agriculture in STEM, not instructional content for the G3-L-8 competency.

copy.en:
Why teach farming in STEM class?

The Philippines' DepEd adds farming and plant science lessons to STEM class so students learn how to grow food sustainably and protect the environment.
copy.tl:
Bakit itinuturo ang agrikultura sa STEM?

Idinagdag ng DepEd ang mga aralin sa agrikultura at agham ng halaman sa STEM curriculum para matuto ang mga estudyante na gumawa ng sustainableng pagkain at alagaan ang kalikasan.
copy.bis:
Ngano gitudlo ang agrikultura sa STEM?

Gidugang sa DepEd ang mga leksyon sa agrikultura ug agham sa tanum sa STEM curriculum aron makakat-on ang mga estudyante og sustainable nga produksyon sa pagkaon ug pag-atiman sa kalikasan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical formula like H₂O tells you which elements and how many atoms of each are in a compound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains what a chemical formula communicates (elements and atom counts) but does not teach writing chemical formulas or chemical names of common covalent compounds such as water, CO2, and ammonia. It is useful background for that competency, not direct instruction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical formula like H₂O tells you which elements and how many atoms of each are in a compound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on compounds having a fixed composition of elements, which is loosely related to pure substances having fixed chemical composition, but it does not describe the properties of pure substances, elements vs compounds, or the unique proton number of an element. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What does a chemical formula like H₂O tell us?

A chemical formula like H₂O tells you which elements and how many atoms of each are in a compound!
copy.tl:
Ano ang sinasabi ng chemical formula tulad ng H₂O?

Ang chemical formula tulad ng H₂O ay nagsasaad kung anong mga elemento at ilang atomo ng bawat isa ang nasa isang compound!
copy.bis:
Unsay gipasabot sa chemical formula sama sa H₂O?

Ang chemical formula sama sa H₂O nagpakita kon unsa nga mga elemento ug pila ka atomo sa matag usa ang naa sa usa ka compound!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They hold chemical potential energy, safely stored right inside their substances
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes chemical potential energy as stored inside substances, but the competency defines potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles. The card does not address kinetic energy or the position-based definition, so it only shares the broad topic of potential energy without directly supporting the competency's specific concept.

copy.en:
What kind of hidden energy is inside your food and car fuel?

They hold chemical potential energy, safely stored right inside their substances to give you power later!
copy.tl:
Anong uri ng nakatagong enerhiya ang nasa loob ng pagkain at gasolina?

May chemical potential energy sila na nakaimbak sa loob ng kanilang mga sangkap para magbigay ng lakas!
copy.bis:
Unang klase sa nakatago nga enerhiya ang naa sa sulod sa pagkaon ug gasolina?

Aduna silay chemical potential energy nga tinipigan sa sulod sa ilang mga sangkap aron mohatag og gahum!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical reaction is the process where starting materials called reactants break and form bonds to become new substances called products.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines a chemical reaction in general. It does not address any specific reaction types (combustion, acids on metals, etc.) or their environmental impacts, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical reaction is the process where starting materials called reactants break and form bonds to become new substances called products.

Safety in numbers! When millions emerge at once, predators simply can't eat them all, so many cicadas survive.
copy.tl:
Bakit sabay-sabay lumalabas ang milyon-milyong kuliglig?

Para sa kaligtasan! Kapag sabay-sabay lumabas ang milyon-milyon, hindi silang lahat makakain ng mga mandaragit, kaya marami ang nakakaligtas.
copy.bis:
Nganong dungan mogula ang minilyon ka kuliglig?

Para sa kaluwasan! Kon dungan mogula ang minilyon, dili sila tanan makaon sa mga manunukob, mao nga daghan ang maluwas.

copy.en: For electricity to flow, it needs a complete closed path called a circuit, going out from the battery and back!
copy.tl: Para dumaloy ang kuryente, kailangan ng kompletong saradong daanan na sirkito, mula sa baterya at pabalik dito!
copy.bis: Aron modagayday ang kuryente, kinahanglan ang tibuok ug sirado nga agianan nga sirkito, gikan sa baterya ug mobalik niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conductors like metal let electricity flow easily. Insulators like plastic block it

assignedReviews.reason: The card defines conductors and insulators, which is background knowledge for testing materials in a circuit, but it does not address designing/constructing a circuit or identifying materials through testing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: which is why wires are coated in plastic to keep us safe!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a safety application (plastic coating on wires) but does not teach that electricity is a flow of electrons, nor does it focus on safe handling measures. The safety note is incidental, not instructional.

copy.en:
What is the difference between a conductor and an insulator?

Conductors like metal let electricity flow easily. Insulators like plastic block it, which is why wires are coated in plastic to keep us safe!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng conductor at insulator?

Ang conductor tulad ng metal ay madaling daluyan ng kuryente. Ang insulator tulad ng plastik ay humaharang, kaya binabalot ng plastik ang alambre para ligtas!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa conductor ug insulator?

Ang conductor sama sa metal sayon agian sa kuryente. Ang insulator sama sa plastik nagbabag, mao nga giputos og plastik ang alambre aron luwas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Current is how much electricity flows past a point every second!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines electric current and its unit (amperes) but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it mention safe measures in handling electricity. It shares the topic of electric current but does not directly support the competency's specific actions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's measured in amperes (A). Bigger current means more charge is flowing through!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery

It only provides a basic definition, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: Current is how much electricity flows past a point every second! It's measured in amperes (A). Bigger current means more charge is flowing through!
copy.tl: Ang current ay kung gaano karaming kuryente ang dumadaloy sa isang punto bawat segundo! Sinusukat ito sa amperes (A). Mas malaking current, mas maraming charge ang dumadaloy!
copy.bis: Ang current mao ang gidaghanon sa kuryente nga moagos sa usa ka punto kada segundo! Gisukod kini sa amperes (A). Mas dako nga current, mas daghang charge ang moagos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Current flows easily through metal conductors like copper! Wires are coated with rubber or plastic insulators that block current so they are safe to hold.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Current flows easily through metal conductors like copper! Wires are coated with rubber or plastic insulators that block current so they are safe to hold.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity

copy.en: Current flows easily through metal conductors like copper! Wires are coated with rubber or plastic insulators that block current so they are safe to hold.
copy.tl: Madaling dumaan ang current sa metal conductors gaya ng copper! Ang mga wire ay binabalot ng rubber o plastic insulators para ligtas hawakan.
copy.bis: Sayon moagi ang current sa metal conductors sama sa copper! Ang mga wire giputos sa rubber o plastic insulators aron luwas hawiran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Higher resistance means smaller current.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic resistance-current relationship but does not involve guided investigations, series/parallel circuits, or varying loads/battery as required by the competency. It provides background knowledge rather than directly supporting the investigative skill.

copy.en: Sometimes current is weak because of resistance, like a blockage. Higher resistance means smaller current. For example, a thin wire has higher resistance than a thick one!
copy.tl: Minsan mahina ang current dahil sa resistance, parang sagabal. Mas mataas ang resistance, mas maliit ang current. Halimbawa, mas mataas ang resistance ng manipis na wire kaysa makapal!
copy.bis: Usahay huyang ang current tungod sa resistance, sama sa babag. Mas taas ang resistance, mas gamay ang current. Pananglitan, mas taas og resistance ang nipis nga wire kaysa baga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Static electricity stays put, like a spark from rubbing a balloon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines static electricity and gives a balloon spark example, but does not support the competency's action of investigating effects of static electricity using common materials (comb, plastic/glass rods, balloons). It provides only a conceptual description, not an investigation or effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Current electricity is a steady flow around a loop, like from a battery.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions current electricity as a flow, but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it address safe measures in handling electricity. It only gives a basic analogy and does not directly support the competency's specific content.

copy.en: Static electricity stays put, like a spark from rubbing a balloon! Current electricity is a steady flow around a loop, like from a battery. Lightning is a sudden static release!
copy.tl: Ang static electricity ay nakatigil, gaya ng spark sa pagkuskos ng balloon! Ang current electricity ay tuloy-tuloy na daloy sa loop, gaya sa battery. Ang kidlat ay biglaang static release!
copy.bis: Ang static electricity nagpabilin, sama sa spark sa pagkuskos sa balloon! Ang current electricity padayon nga agos sa loop, sama sa battery. Ang kilat kalit nga static release!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: energy transforms! Chemical energy in the battery becomes electrical energy. Then in the bulb, it turns into light and heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes energy changing from one form to another (chemical to electrical to light and heat) but does not state that energy can cause change, which is the core of G4-F-9. It only mentions light and heat as forms, not as evidence of energy causing change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Then in the bulb, it turns into light and heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light and heat as outputs of a bulb in a circuit, but it does not identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, home, or community. It is a specific circuit example, not a survey of sources and uses.

copy.en: In a circuit, energy transforms! Chemical energy in the battery becomes electrical energy. Then in the bulb, it turns into light and heat!
copy.tl: Sa isang circuit, nagbabago ang anyo ng enerhiya! Ang kemikal na enerhiya sa baterya ay nagiging elektrikal na enerhiya. Pagkatapos sa bombilya, nagiging ilaw at init ito!
copy.bis: Sa usa ka circuit, mausab ang porma sa enerhiya! Ang kemikal nga enerhiya sa baterya nahimong elektrikal nga enerhiya. Dayon sa bombilya, nahimo kini nga kahayag ug kainit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its terminal voltage drops because of internal resistance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a single phenomenon (voltage drop due to internal resistance) but does not support the competency's focus on guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series/parallel circuits. It provides no circuit assembly, no investigation, and no relationship inference.

copy.en: When a battery gives out a big current, its terminal voltage drops because of internal resistance. That's why old batteries lose voltage when connected to a heavy load!
copy.tl: Kapag malaki ang kuryenteng kinukuha sa baterya, bumababa ang terminal voltage nito dahil sa panloob na resistensya. Kaya pala bumababa ang boltahe ng lumang baterya kapag naka-connect sa mabigat na load!
copy.bis: Kung moduso ug dako nga kuryente ang baterya, moubos ang terminal voltage niini tungod sa panloob nga resistensya. Mao ni ang rason nganong moubos ang boltahe sa karaan nga baterya inig-konekta sa mabigat nga load!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heavy appliances like air conditioners and ovens need their own dedicated circuit to avoid overloading a breaker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses home branch circuits and breaker overload, but does not address generation of high voltage electricity, power plants, substations, or electric meters, which are the core of G10-F-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Philippine homes have several branch circuits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to recognize the advantages and limitations of using series or parallel circuits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions branch circuits but does not discuss series vs parallel circuits, their advantages/limitations, or a class discussion. It is about load balancing in home wiring, not the comparison of circuit configurations.

copy.en: Philippine homes have several branch circuits — heavy appliances like air conditioners and ovens need their own dedicated circuit to avoid overloading a breaker.
copy.tl: May ilang branch circuit ang mga bahay sa Pilipinas — kailangan ng sariling dedicated circuit ang mabibigat na appliance tulad ng aircon at oven para hindi ma-overload ang breaker.
copy.bis: Adunay daghang branch circuit ang mga balay sa Pilipinas — kinahanglan og kaugalingong dedicated circuit ang mabig-at nga appliance sama sa aircon ug oven aron dili ma-overload ang breaker.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: every connection must be clean and tight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a troubleshooting tip about loose connections causing flicker, but does not teach how to assemble or draw a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb. It is background knowledge about circuit reliability, not direct instruction for the assembly/drawing skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: every connection must be clean and tight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address designing/constructing a circuit to test conductivity of materials. It only mentions connection tightness, which is unrelated to identifying conductors/insulators.

copy.en: For a circuit to work, every connection must be clean and tight! If a connection is loose, the bulb might flicker or stop lighting altogether.
copy.tl: Para gumana ang circuit, dapat malinis at mahigpit ang bawat koneksyon! Kung maluwag ang dikit, maaaring kumikislap o tuluyang mamatay ang bombilya.
copy.bis: Aron mogana ang circuit, kinahanglan limpyo ug hugot ang matag koneksyon! Kung luag ang dikit, mahimong magkidlap o hingpit nga mapalong ang bombilya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a straight line through the origin! The slope of that line equals the conductor's resistance — that's Ohm's Law in action!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the Ohm's law relationship (V = IR) for an ohmic conductor, but the competency requires guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery. The card does not address series/parallel circuits, varying loads, or the investigative process; it only presents a general graph fact.

copy.en:
What does the graph of voltage against current look like for an ohmic conductor?

It's a straight line through the origin! The slope of that line equals the conductor's resistance — that's Ohm's Law in action!
copy.tl:
Ano ang itsura ng graph ng boltahe laban sa kuryente para sa isang ohmic conductor?

Ito ay isang tuwid na guhit na dumadaan sa simula! Ang slope ng guhit ay katumbas ng resistensya ng conductor — ganito gumagana ang Ohm's Law!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang porma sa graph sa boltahe batok sa kuryente para sa usa ka ohmic conductor?

Kini usa ka tuwid nga guhit nga moagi sa simula! Ang slope sa guhit katumbas sa resistensya sa conductor — mao ni ang Ohm's Law nga nagtrabaho!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's how much a material fights the flow of current! Thick, short wires have low resistance, while thin, long wires have higher resistance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines electrical resistance and notes how wire thickness and length affect it, which is background knowledge for understanding resistance. However, the competency requires guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits; the card does not address current, voltage, circuits, or the investigative relationship.

copy.en:
What is electrical resistance?

It's how much a material fights the flow of current! Thick, short wires have low resistance, while thin, long wires have higher resistance.
copy.tl:
Ano ang electrical resistance?

Ito ay kung gaano pinaglabanan ng isang materyales ang agos ng kuryente! Ang makapal at maikling kawad ay may mababang resistensya, habang ang manipis at mahabang kawad ay may mataas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang electrical resistance?

Mao kini kung unsa ka dako ang pagkontra sa materyales sa agos sa kuryente! Ang baga ug mubo nga kawad adunay ubos nga resistensya, samtang ang nipis ug taas nga kawad adunay mas taas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about current in a series circuit. The competency requires guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery. The card does not address voltage, resistance, parallel circuits, or any investigative/inference process, so it only shares vocabulary and a basic series-circuit property without directly supporting the competency's skill.

copy.en: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point — because there is only one path for electrons to flow, the same amount of current passes through every component.
copy.tl: Sa isang series circuit, ang kuryente ay pareho sa lahat ng dako — dahil iisa lamang ang daan ng electrons, parehong dami ng kuryente ang dumadaan sa bawat bahagi.
copy.bis: Sa usa ka series circuit, ang kuryente pareho sa tanan nga bahin — tungod kay usa lamang ang agianan alang sa mga electrons, mao rang dami sa kuryente ang moagi sa matag parte.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer

copy.en: In a flashlight, wires join the battery, switch, and bulb! The battery gives energy, the switch controls the path, and the bulb lights up.
copy.tl: Sa lampara, pinagdudugtong ng mga alambre ang baterya, switch, at bombilya! Nagbibigay ng enerhiya ang baterya, kinokontrol ng switch ang daanan, at nagliliwanag ang bombilya.
copy.bis: Sa flashlight, gidugtong sa mga alambre ang baterya, switch, ug bombilya! Naghatag og enerhiya ang baterya, nagkontrol ang switch sa agianan, ug modan-ag ang bombilya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A two-way switch lets you do this!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of a two-way switch for controlling one light from two locations, but does not involve assembling or drawing a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb as required by the competency. It is only topically related to circuits.

copy.en:
How can you control one light from two different spots?

A two-way switch lets you do this! It is used in staircases and hallways so you can turn the light on or off from either end.
copy.tl:
Paano kontrolin ang isang ilaw mula sa dalawang lugar?

Gamitin ang two-way switch! Ginagamit ito sa hagdan at pasilyo para ma-on o ma-off mo ang ilaw kahit saan ka sa dulo nito.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkontrol sa usa ka suga gikan sa duha ka lugar?

Gamita ang two-way switch! Gigamit ni sa hagdan ug pasilyo aron ma-on o ma-off nimo ang suga bisan asa ka sa ulohang dapit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voltage measures how strongly a battery pushes the current!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines voltage as the battery's push and its unit (volts), with an AA battery example. It does not address the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance, nor series/parallel circuits or guided investigations, which are the core of the competency. The definition is useful background but not direct instructional support.

copy.en: Voltage measures how strongly a battery pushes the current! It's measured in volts. A common AA battery? Just 1.5 volts!
copy.tl: Ang voltage ay sumusukat kung gaano lakas ang pagtulak ng baterya sa kuryente! Sinusukat ito sa volts. Ang karaniwang AA battery? 1.5 volts lang!
copy.bis: Ang voltage nagsukod kung pila kusog ang pagduso sa baterya sa kuryente! Gisukod kini sa volts. Ang kasagaran nga AA battery? 1.5 volts ra!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because metal is a conductor! Electricity flows through it easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that metal is a conductor and explains why wires are made of metal, but it does not involve designing or constructing a circuit, nor does it guide identification of materials that conduct or do not conduct electricity. It only provides background knowledge about conductors, not the investigative skill required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why are wires made of metal like copper?

Because metal is a conductor! Electricity flows through it easily to connect all the parts of the circuit.
copy.tl:
Bakit gawa sa metal tulad ng tanso ang mga alambre?

Dahil ang metal ay isang conductor! Madaling dumaloy ang kuryente dito para iugnay ang lahat ng bahagi ng circuit.
copy.bis:
Nganong hinimo sa metal sama sa tanso ang mga alambre?

Tungod kay ang metal usa ka conductor! Sayon nga moagos ang kuryente niini aron idugtong ang tanang bahin sa circuit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy like feathers! They show up in fair weather but can hint a change is coming.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific cloud type (cirrus) and its weather association, but does not teach cloud cover as a basic weather characteristic or how to identify/describe weather characteristics such as air temperature, wind, humidity, etc. It shares vocabulary (clouds, weather) but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy like feathers! They show up in fair weather but can hint a change is coming.
copy.tl: Ang cirrus clouds ay manipis at parang balahibo! Lumalabas sila sa magandang panahon pero pwedeng tanda ng paparating na pagbabago.
copy.bis: Ang cirrus clouds nipis ug morag balhibo! Motungha sila sa maayong panahon apan mahimong timaan nga adunay umaabot nga kausaban.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thin, feathery cirrus clouds float so high where it's freezing cold that they're made of tiny ice crystals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific cloud type (cirrus) and its composition, which touches on cloud cover as a weather characteristic. However, the competency asks students to identify basic weather characteristics (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, cloud cover) as a set. The card does not teach what cloud cover is as a weather characteristic, nor does it help identify it among other characteristics. It is only tangentially related to cloud cover.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thin, feathery cirrus clouds float so high where it's freezing cold that they're made of tiny ice crystals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on observing and recording changes in weather over time and describing types/patterns of local weather. The card gives a static fact about cirrus clouds, not about weather changes, patterns, or local weather observation. It does not support the skill of observing/recording weather changes or describing weather patterns.

copy.en: Thin, feathery cirrus clouds float so high where it's freezing cold that they're made of tiny ice crystals, not water droplets — the wind blows them into hair-like wisps!
copy.tl: Ang manipis at parang balahibong cirrus cloud ay napakataas kung saan napakalamig, kaya gawa sila sa maliliit na kristal ng yelo, hindi patak ng tubig — iinihip ng hangin sa hugis-buhok!
copy.bis: Ang manipis ug morag balhibo nga cirrus cloud taas kaayo diin bugnaw kaayo — hinimo sa gagmay nga kristal sa yelo, dili tulo sa tubig. Gipahuyop sa hangin sa porma nga buhok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cirrus clouds are made of tiny ice crystals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a fact about cirrus cloud composition, not instruction on identifying basic weather characteristics such as cloud cover, temperature, or humidity. It shares the topic of clouds but does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying weather descriptors.

copy.en: Cirrus clouds are made of tiny ice crystals because it's super cold way up high where they form!
copy.tl: Ang cirrus clouds ay gawa sa maliliit na ice crystals dahil napakalamig sa taas kung saan sila nabubuo!
copy.bis: Ang cirrus clouds hinimo gikan sa gagmay nga ice crystals tungod kay bugnaw kaayo sa taas diin sila maporma!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why cirrus clouds are thin and look like strands of hair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the meaning of the word 'cirrus' and describes the appearance of cirrus clouds. It does not teach students to identify basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, or cloud cover as a measurable weather descriptor. The content is only tangentially related to clouds, which are part of weather, but it does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en:
What does 'cirrus' mean?

It means a curl of hair! That's why cirrus clouds are thin and look like strands of hair.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng 'cirrus'?

Kulot ng buhok! Kaya ang cirrus na ulap ay manipis at parang mga hibla ng buhok.
copy.bis:
Unsay pasabot sa 'cirrus'?

Kulot sa buhok! Mao nga ang cirrus nga panganod nipis ug morag mga hilo sa buhok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cirrus are thin, wispy clouds that form very high in the sky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a type of cloud, which is tangentially related to cloud cover as a weather characteristic, but it does not identify cloud cover or other basic weather characteristics as described in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made of tiny ice crystals instead of water droplets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made of tiny ice crystals instead of water droplets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas

copy.en: Cirrus are thin, wispy clouds that form very high in the sky and are made of tiny ice crystals instead of water droplets!
copy.tl: Ang cirrus ay manipis at wispy na ulap na nasa pinakamataas na bahagi ng kalangitan, at gawa sa maliliit na ice crystals imbes na water droplets!
copy.bis: Ang cirrus mga nipis ug wispy nga panganod nga anaa sa kinatas-ang bahin sa langit, ug hinimo sa gagmayng ice crystals imbis water droplets!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They contain citric acid, which is the secret ingredient that makes them taste sour.

copy.en:
What is a climax community?

A climax community is the most stable grouping of species reached after a long process of change, like a mature rainforest that now shifts only slowly.
copy.tl:
Ano ang climax community?

Ang climax community ay ang pinaka-stable na kalipunan ng species pagkatapos ng matagal na proseso ng pagbabago, tulad ng isang mature na rainforest na dahan-dahan na lang nagbabago.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang climax community?

Ang climax community mao ang labing lig-on nga grupo sa species human sa dugay nga proseso sa kausaban, sama sa hamtong nga rainforest nga hinay na lang mausab.

Who cleans our canals before the rainy season?

City workers! They remove built-up mud and trash so water flows well again and floods are avoided.

Sino ang naglilinis ng kanal bago ang tag-ulan?

Mga city workers! Inaalis nila ang naipong putik at basura para makadaloy nang maayos ang tubig at maiwasan ang baha.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naglimpyo sa kanal sa dili pa moabot ang tag-ulan?

Mga city workers! Ilang kuhaon ang natapok nga lapok ug basura aron makadagayday na usab ang tubig ug malikayan ang baha.

Can liquid cooking oil clog drains too?

Yes! When poured down the sink, cooking oil hardens and sticks inside the pipe, slowly blocking the water flow!
copy.tl:
Nakakabara ba ang cooking oil sa mga kanal?

Oo! Kapag ibinuhos sa lababo, tumitigas at dumidikit ang cooking oil sa loob ng tubo, unti-unti nitong nababara ang daloy ng tubig!
copy.bis:
Makababag ba ang cooking oil sa mga kanal?

Oo! Kung ibubo sa lababo, motig-a ug motapot ang cooking oil sulod sa tubo, hinay-hinay kining makababag sa dagayday sa tubig!

copy.en:
Why does Manila flood so easily?

Many of Manila's narrow esteros get blocked by garbage. This causes fast flooding even in light rain, especially in low areas.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabilis bumaha sa Maynila?

Maraming makitid na estero sa Maynila ang nababara ng basura. Kaya mabilis bumaha kahit sa banayad na ulan, lalo na sa mababang lugar.
copy.bis:
Ngano paspas mobaha sa Manila?

Daghang sigpit nga estero sa Manila mababagan sa basura. Paspas mobaha bisan sa hinay nga ulan, ilabi na sa ubos nga lugar.

copy.bis: Kung husto ang paglain sa basura, mas gamay ang moadto sa kanal! Makatabang kini aron dili mababagan ang agianan ug malikayan ang baha.

Is trash the only thing that clogs drains?

Nope! Mud and sand from rain settle at the bottom. Over time, this thick layer shrinks the water's path!
copy.tl:
Basura lang ba ang bumabara sa mga kanal?

Hindi! Ang putik at buhangin mula sa ulan ay naiipon sa ilalim. Lumalapot ito at lumiliit ang daanan ng tubig!
copy.bis:
Basura ra ba ang makababag sa mga kanal?

Dili! Ang lapok ug balas gikan sa ulan hinay-hinay nga matapok sa ilalom. Mobaga kini ug mogamay ang agianan sa tubig!

copy.tl: Ang mabahong amoy mula sa kanal ay senyales na barado ito! Kapag tumigil ang tubig at nabulok ang basura sa loob, lumalabas ang masamang amoy — oras na para linisin ito!
copy.bis: Ang baho gikan sa kanal timaan nga mababagan kini! Kung mohunong ang tubig ug madunot ang basura sa sulod, mogawas ang baho — oras na para limpyohan kini!
